audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer chart gives Irelia levels 1-5 and calls 6 onward 'Skill'; content and packet read Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Irelia/Ekko/Ekko.
audit.why: Content matches the packet and the kit. Bladesurge is 600 range against a 1075 Q and only refreshes off a Mark or a kill, so levels 1-4 are genuinely even; level 6 is hers because Vanguard's Edge Marks and refreshes the dash; from first item Ekko's string kills before her resets accumulate.
audit.corrected: Full rows aligned to content with each why rewritten to argue its own verdict.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content whys are shifted one row off their labels: whys[4] sits on the Level 6 row but reads 'Levels 4-5 tip to Irelia', and whys[5] sits on the First item row but reads 'Level 6 swings to Ekko'. The 'mid' paragraph also credits Ekko with 'Ionian Fervor', which is Irelia's passive.
audit.why: The reader sees a stage label and a sentence about a different stage, and a power curve attributed to the wrong champion.
audit.corrected: whys[4] rewritten as the level 6 verdict (Vanguard's Edge Marks, Mark refreshes Bladesurge), whys[5] as the first-item verdict, and the 'mid' paragraph rebuilt without the misattributed passive.

audit.whatIsWrong: Flawless Duet GROUNDS as well as stuns — it switches off Ekko's E, his only escape at 325 range — and Bladesurge heals Irelia on every cast. Neither reached the page.
audit.why: Riot's kit carries grounding + hardCC on her E and heal on her Q; both missingInteractions entries flag exactly these.
audit.corrected: cooldowns, tradeBad, breakdown.trading, dontsFull[2].d and report[8].t now state the grounding, the Bladesurge heal and the Oblivion Orb timing.

audit.why: It is the field that must hold real cooldowns.
audit.corrected: Now carries Flawless Duet 16s, Bladesurge 10s (refreshing on a Marked target), Vanguard's Edge 125s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Eleven fields called Irelia 'he/his/him'; dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string and dontsFull[2].d the tradeBad string under unrelated titles.
audit.why: champ-gender.js marks irelia female, and the bullet bodies were pasted from the trade fields.
audit.corrected: All flagged non-report fields rewritten; two report entries fixed within the cap, the rest listed in notes.

edits.before: Irelia
edits.after: Skill

edits.before: Q the wave and his toes — the return pass chunks; learn the slow zone's drag on his dodge patterns.
edits.after: Q both passes at 1075 range — Bladesurge is 600 and only refreshes off a Mark or a minion kill.

edits.before: Irelia
edits.after: Skill

edits.before: E blink-strike window opens: Q-E-auto is your first real trade and the third passive hit stings already.
edits.after: E opens the blink-strike, but Flawless Duet grounds you — never spend the dash while her E is loaded.

edits.before: Irelia
edits.after: Skill

edits.before: W zone games begin: drop it on his retreat line BEFORE trading and the stun finds him mid-regret.
edits.after: Drop W on her approach line before trading — her stun is 16s at rank 1 and it is the whole all-in.

edits.before: Irelia
edits.after: Skill

edits.before: Three-hit trades on cooldown — Q in, E the gap, passive proc, walk. Bank the tempo for 6.
edits.after: Q in, E the gap, passive proc, walk — Bladesurge heals her, so end it before she gets a reset.

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Irelia

edits.before: Chronobreak online — your aggression gets a save file. Trade like the rewind exists, because it does.
edits.after: Vanguard's Edge Marks you at 950 and a Mark refreshes Bladesurge — her chain beats your rewind here.

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Ekko

edits.before: First item spike: the full string deletes half bars and the rewind erases the counter-argument.
edits.after: First item: the string kills before her Q resets stack, and 16s of Flawless Duet is a long wait.

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Ekko

edits.before: Late Ekko picks and survives: dive the carry, W the peel, and Chronobreak out of whatever they answered with.
edits.after: Late you take the pick and rewind out; her ultimate leaves a wall, so open the fight from her side of it.

edits.before: - Irelia Flawless Duet (Stun): matchup-defining — Her stun setup — dodge it and the dive falls apart. It governs your forward steps. - R Chronobreak spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Flawless Duet is 16s at rank 1 and grounds as well as stuns — it switches off your E, so it, not her health bar, sets your timing. - Bladesurge is 10s but refreshes on a Marked target. - Vanguard's Edge is 125s.

edits.before: He brawls, you phase — three hits and gone, with a rewind for the one time the door closes too slow.
edits.after: She brawls, you phase — three hits and gone, with a rewind for the one time the door closes too slow.

edits.before: Q through him, E the gap, passive third hit, walk out through the slow — the full string chunks and the return pass pays the exit.
edits.after: Q through her, E the gap, passive third hit, then leave early — Bladesurge heals her, so a long trade pays her back.

edits.before: Blinking in with R down against a loaded kit — Ekko without the rewind is a mid laner doing parkour at a funeral.
edits.after: Dashing in with Flawless Duet loaded — it grounds as well as stuns, so your E is gone and her chain starts.

edits.before: Good trade: Q through him, E the gap, passive third hit, walk out through the slow — the full string chunks and the return pass pays the exit. Bad trade: Blinking in with R down against a loaded kit — Ekko without the rewind is a mid laner doing parkour at a funeral.
edits.after: Good trade: Q through her, E the gap, passive third hit, then leave early — Bladesurge heals her, so a long trade pays her back. Bad trade: dashing in with Flawless Duet loaded — it grounds and stuns, so your E is off and her reset chain starts.

edits.before: Best wave: a Q-cleared push that crashes while your hologram bank stays healthy — tempo with insurance. Worst wave: a frozen wave near his tower with E down — no blink, no string, no business being there. Crash timing: shove with a destination in mind; mid waves are bus tickets, not chores.
edits.after: Best wave: a Q-cleared push that crashes while your hologram bank stays healthy — tempo with insurance. Worst wave: a frozen wave near her tower with E down — no blink, no exit, and every minion a Bladesurge reset. Crash timing: shove with a destination in mind; mid waves are bus tickets, not chores.

edits.before: Irelia wins by landing Flawless Duet (Stun), denying your pattern, and cashing the all-in before your pattern matures.
edits.after: Irelia wins by grounding your E with Flawless Duet, chaining Bladesurge off her Marks, and healing through the trade.

edits.before: Carry through insured dives — one carry per rewind cycle; your job is spending R as a weapon, not an apology.
edits.after: Carry on the 16s Flawless Duet downtime — without the stun she has to walk into your string on foot.

edits.before: Her stun setup — dodge it and the dive falls apart. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Flawless Duet is 16s at rank 1 — with it down she cannot open the all-in. Wait for it, then go.

edits.before: Q through him, E the gap, passive third hit, walk out through the slow — the full string chunks and the return pass pays the exit.
edits.after: Drop the anomaly behind you before she steps up — Bladesurge only reaches 600, and the stun catches her dash home.

edits.before: Trade inside his wave
edits.after: Trade inside her wave

edits.before: Blinking in with R down against a loaded kit — Ekko without the rewind is a mid laner doing parkour at a funeral.
edits.after: Every minion is a Bladesurge reset at 600 range — inside her wave she gets a free chain of dashes onto you.

edits.before: He brawls, you phase — three hits and gone, with a rewind for the one time the door closes too slow.
edits.after: She brawls, you phase — three hits and gone, with a rewind for the one time the door closes too slow.

edits.before: Start Doran's Shield or Ring + pots. Hextech Rocketbelt or Stormsurge line, Sorcerer's, then Zhonya's-Lich Bane paths. Add anti-heal early into his sustain.
edits.after: Start Doran's Shield + pots. Hextech Rocketbelt or Stormsurge, Sorcerer's, then Zhonya's — and buy Oblivion Orb early, because Bladesurge heals her on every reset.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 tip to Irelia because her Ionian Fervor stacking plus cheap Q resets let her force all-ins Ekko can't yet answer with a reliable stun.
edits.after: Level 6 still tips to Irelia: Vanguard's Edge Marks you and a Mark refreshes Bladesurge, so her chain keeps coming while your rewind is still 110s.

edits.before: Level 6 swings to Ekko since Chronobreak gives you a genuine escape/reset tool while Irelia's ultimate offers no comparable burst spike, letting your base kit catch up.
edits.after: Your first item swings it: Chronobreak plus the full string kills her before the Q resets accumulate, and Vanguard's Edge is peel rather than a burst spike.

edits.before: Levels 3-4 favor Irelia if she gets clean Q resets off minions to true-damage-proc into an all-in, but by level 5 her ability to just walk you down fades since your Parallel Convergence threat zone covers your farm; level 6 flips fully your way because Ekko's Ionian Fervor-adjusted power curve catches up and she has no ultimate spike to counter your Chronobreak setup.
edits.after: Levels 3-4 favour Irelia when she gets clean Bladesurge resets off minions to chain into an all-in, but by level 5 her ability to simply walk you down fades since your Parallel Convergence threat zone covers your farm; level 6 stays hers because Vanguard's Edge Marks you for another free dash, and it is your first item that finally answers the chain.

notes: Content win[] already matched the packet levelChart, so the side edits bring only the full layer into line and no paired win[N] edit exists to propose. The content whys were shifted one row off their labels (whys[4] on the Level 6 row described levels 4-5; whys[5] on the First item row described level 6) — rewritten to their own rows rather than moving any side, since content and packet agree on the sides. The 'mid' paragraph credited Ekko with 'Ionian Fervor', which is Irelia's passive; removed. MISGENDER remains in report[3].t, report[4].t and report[11].t — outside the two-report cap, all plain he/his/him -> she/her swaps. packet.suspectNames flags 'Drive Resonance'/'Z-Drive Resonance' and 'Save Parallel Convergence' — both are correct names for Ekko's own passive and W, FALSE POSITIVES.
